[LDET.3.3a.7] **Compile-time evaluation into a bundle-bound value.** A value
computed at **compile time** whose result is serialized into the bundle — a
constant folded into the program image, a lowered DSC atom, a representative
value, a numeric literal apportioned to a fixed-point scale — **MUST** be
produced by the **EXACT-class** machinery of this registry: exact
integer/rational arithmetic, or the correctly-rounded IEEE operations of
[LDET.3.3a.4]. It **MUST NOT** be produced by the compiler host's native
floating point — host `libm` transcendentals, extended-precision or
FMA-contracted evaluation, or locale-dependent decimal parsing — because **the
compiler host is not a conforming target** ([LDET.2.3]), and a value it rounds
differently from a conforming engine is a silent cross-target divergence baked
permanently into the bundle. *Instance:* a duration literal apportioned to
nanoseconds, or a unit-conversion factor folded into a threshold, is computed in
exact integer/rational arithmetic and quantised once by round-half-to-even —
never host `double`. A transcendental the compiler folds is the correctly-rounded
value [LEXP.3.9.2] requires, at [LEXP.3.9.3]'s special values, computed in
round-to-nearest-even ([LDET.3.6.1]) — the same bits a conforming engine
returns. (Since v1 admits only EXACT constructs, every compile-time
bundle-bound value is covered by this clause directly.)
